**Tests.** The three Python tests are Catch2 cases of `tests/devtools/speccheck_tests.cpp`, in the one devtools executable, with the same synthetic inputs and the same injected defects: two files claiming one `TEST_CASE` id; one id defined in two specification files, as a table row and as a bullet; a lettered acceptance row, and a requirement genuinely undischarged. Each ctest keeps its name and runs the tag of the test it replaces; `speccheck.behaviour` runs the cases that came with the port (the printed text of a run, derived from the Python's print statements; every kind of finding; the refusals and their exit codes; universal newlines; what the tree walk reads; each scanner against its pattern) and `speccheck.real_tree` is gate 7's own run as a test. One devkit case covers the two new helpers. **Rule 5** (`C3_rule5_injected_defects.txt`): 90 defects injected into `speccheck.cpp`, run against the final tests, 90 caught; the first run (89 defects) found the tests thin in two places — a range's last number not required to end at a word boundary, and a definition cell without its closing backtick — and each got cases; none was left as a note.

### 41.10 Group C3's runner finding — a directory's size, and what /tmp is

**The run (read by the maintainer, 2026-10-07).** Run 37491731484, of `1777172` (C3), is the first run on a RESTORED cache ("Cache restored successfully", key `manifest-c18eb438…`), so the restore path is proven. It passed 655 of 656 tests and failed one case of `speccheck.behaviour`, "the tree-wide scan: the root's own build*/ and data/ are not read, nested ones are, links are not followed, and a file that is not UTF-8 is skipped", at its last two assertions — `t.run({"--quiet"}).code == kOk` and `== kGaps`, both with the expansion `70 == …`: the tool's internal-error exit. The other 22 cases of the tag passed, and `speccheck.real_tree` passed on the runner. Every local run had passed: this machine's, the maintainer's isolated-export run, and mine under g++-13.

**The cause, reproduced.** The case makes a DIRECTORY named `odd.cpp` (a source tree may hold one; `*.cpp` matches by name) and the tool reads every match. `devkit::read_bytes` learned that a path was no file from the size it read — seek to the end, tell. **tmpfs answers −1 for a directory**, which became the refusal "it is not a regular file" that the tool skips; **ext4 — the runner's `/tmp` is a disk — answers 9 223 372 036 854 775 807 (2^63 − 1)**; a vector of that size throws `std::bad_alloc`, which is no `std::runtime_error`, and the tool's catch-all wrote "internal error: std::bad_alloc" and exited 70. The suspects named for the failure — the case's link, its unreadable-looking file, its non-UTF-8 file — were not it. Reproduced here with the very same test binary run under `TMPDIR=/var/tmp` (this machine's ext4; the default `/tmp` is a tmpfs, which is why every local run passed): the same two assertions fail with `70 == 0` and `70 == 1`, and the tool run by hand on such a tree prints `speccheck: internal error: std::bad_alloc`. A ten-line probe prints what `tellg` says after `seekg(end)` of the directory: −1 on tmpfs, 9223372036854775807 on ext4.

**The fix, in the library under the tool and in the tool.** (1) `devkit::read_bytes` decides by KIND before it opens anything: `status` (following a link, as opening does) refuses what is not a regular file in the same words as before, "it is not a regular file", and what is not there with the system's own reason; and a file larger than the memory there is is a refusal that names it ("too large to read into memory"), never a `std::bad_alloc` out of a tool. A FIFO is no longer opened at all (opening one waits for a writer for ever). (2) `speccheck`'s scan skips what is not a regular file BY RULE, before it reads — a directory called `x.cpp`, a link to one, a link to nothing, a FIFO — instead of by what reading one happens to do on a filesystem; a link to a regular file is read through, as pathlib read it. The rule behind both: **a scan of a tree must never exit 70 for what it finds there; it refuses or skips by a stated rule.**

**Tests.** `tools/devkit/tests/fs_tests.cpp` (four devkit cases: a directory, a FIFO, a link to a directory, a link to nothing, a missing file, a regular file, an empty one, a link to a regular file, an unreadable file when not run as root, and a sparse file of 2^62 bytes, skipped where the filesystem will not make one — ext4 will not, tmpfs does); and the speccheck case extended with the directory's link, a dangling link, a FIFO and a link to a regular file. They hold on every filesystem, and the old code passed them only on tmpfs: the old failure shows under a `TMPDIR` on a disk, which is how it was reproduced and how the fix was rehearsed. The whole devtools executable (114 cases) was also run under `TMPDIR=/var/tmp`: all pass, the one skip being the 2^62 file. **Rule 5** (`C4_rule5_runner_fix.txt` in the report's files): nine defects, run under the ext4 temporary directory. Caught: the status error not checked, the regular-file check removed (which also hangs on the FIFO and is killed by the timeout), `symlink_status` in place of `status`, a status error reported as "not regular", a regular check that admits directories, and the scan's rule inverted. The `bad_alloc` handler removed survives under ext4 — the 2^62 case is skipped there — and is caught on tmpfs, so the pair of runs is the evidence. Two are equivalent, and said so: the negative-size check (a regular file never has one now) and the scan's own rule (`read_bytes` refuses the same kinds; the rule stays so that the scan does not depend on it).

**What this cannot show from here.** That the runner passes: the next run is the test. And the general lesson, which is the reason it is written down: a test that makes a filesystem object and reads the system's answer depends on the filesystem under `/tmp`. The other tests of this tree that touch the filesystem passed on the runner and under `TMPDIR` on a disk here; a new test that makes a special file is run both ways.

### 41.11 Group C4 — the budget-row checker in C++, and speccheck's `(partial` finding

**What.** `tools/budgetcheck.cpp` (+ `.hpp`) replaces `tools/budgetcheck.py`; `ci.sh`'s gate 8 runs the built tool (`$BUILD/tools/budgetcheck --quiet`) and so does the ctest `budget.arithmetic`; `budgetcheck.py` and `tests/test_budgetcheck.py` are removed in the same commit. The Python's regular expressions — the row pattern, `EXPR`, `PROSE`, `NUM` and the four normalising substitutions — are hand-written scanners over UTF-8 text with Python's Unicode-aware `\s` and `\d`, exposed (`scan::*`, `parse_unit`, `parse_number`, `parse_term`, `significant_tolerance`, `check_row`) so that each is tested against the semantics of the code it replaces; the arithmetic is the Python's operation for operation (`float()` is `strtod`, `**` is `pow`, `math.log10` and `math.floor` are `log10` and `floor`, the tolerance is `(0.5 * 10^k) * 1.001`, the quantities multiply left to right, nothing is fused: `-ffp-contract=off` on the tool's two targets). The devkit gains the `str` methods it needed (`strip_py`, `lstrip_py`, `lstrip_chars_py`, `split_py` and `code_point_at` in `pytext`; `py_format_g` in `pyfmt`).

**The proof (D1), registered before any C++ of the tool existed** (`C4_budgetcheck_proof_registration.txt`, with the byte target `C4_budgetcheck_baseline_stdout.txt`). budgetcheck writes no file; its product is what it PRINTS, and with `--quiet` (gate 8, `budget.arithmetic`) that is three lines — 128 bytes, SHA-256 `b42da184…ecd8d` — whose committed record is gate 8's section of the safety-net run at `acac318` (and, byte for byte, of every ci run since). The substitution list was EMPTY (the output holds no path, date or generator name). The port printed those 128 bytes, with exit 0 and an empty standard error, **on its first and only comparison** (`C4_budgetcheck_proof_result.txt`). The counts agree with a count made with the shell before any C++ existed: 103 rows, 71 with a `= **result**` expression, 32 without, 6 rows with more than one expression. The comparison was repeated once on the final binary after the redundant parts of the code were removed (the same result; recorded beside the first).

**What the committed record does not hold, and what stands in for it.** The per-row lines of a run without `--quiet` and the text of any failure: no ci log, report or file has them, and the Python was not run beside the port. They stand on (a) the readings of the Python, with tests whose expectations are derived by hand from its print statements and its arithmetic (each printed text in the tests is such, and the one hand-derived expectation that was wrong — a blank between two digits is dropped by the grouping step before the `10^` fold reads it — was a defect of the test, found because the port followed the Python's order of steps); (b) the controls registered before the port: **each of the 103 real rows alone** (71 with arithmetic and 32 with none, row by row: the baseline's counts) and **each of the 71 with its first stated result made wrong** (the digit 9 put before its first digit), every one of which must fail as ARITHMETIC WRONG, and all do, so no row is skipped or loosened; they remain as the ctest `budgetcheck.real_tree`; (c) the first record of the tool's non-quiet output on the real tree (`C4_budgetcheck_real_tree_nonquiet.txt`: 80 `ok` lines and 3 `note` lines), read against the rows — the FIRST such record, a regression record from now on and not a proof against the Python; (d) rule 5.

**Differences from the Python, deliberate, each said in the tool's header.** Where the Python raised `OverflowError` (a unit raised to a power the double cannot hold, `km^200`; a stated value that is infinite, `1e999`; a stated unit whose scale underflows to zero, `fm^30`, which it divided by) a traceback became an UNPARSEABLE finding, exit 2; its own `ValueError` texts are interpreter-version text, so where they would appear (an empty `max()`) the tool's words stand in; an exponent whose magnitude exceeds a million is refused (the Python's integers have no limit, this tool's are 64 bits); a specification that is not UTF-8, or is no file, is REFUSED, exit 2; the messages name `budgetcheck`; argparse's abbreviations are not accepted and `-h` prints the tool's own text. **Kept as they are — found by reading the Python, reported to the maintainer, not fixed:** a specification directory that is absent or holds no `SPEC-*.md` passes with "0 budget rows" (a checker that reports success over rows it never read is the very failure this tool was built against: the maintainer's ruling is awaited); `10^+3` reads as 10 (the plus sign makes `^+3` a dimensionless "unit" raised to 3); a unit token `m^` reads as `m`; `int()`'s digit separators (`m^1_0`) are read; the tolerance of a stated zero is 0.5 in the stated units (so `0.4 mm = **0 mm**` passes); a left side that is `NaN` passes. **CHANGED in the follow-up (§41.12), on the maintainer's rulings of 2026-10-07: all of them but the tolerance of a stated zero are now refused (UNPARSEABLE, or the empty directory refused as speccheck refuses it); the text above is kept as it was written.**

**speccheck's `(partial` finding — a deliberate change of behaviour, on the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-07.** A `(partial` Coverage row says that a test covers the rest of the requirement. When it names a requirement no acceptance row discharges, group C3 refused (one line, exit 1) where the Python's partition `assert` had crashed (§41.9). It is now REPORTED: one named finding per requirement — the specification, the identifier, and the row's own first cell, with what to do — on standard error whatever `--quiet` says, a line in the block, exit 1. The requirement is counted once: as uncovered, or as excused whole if an ordinary row also excuses it, which is the second route to the Python's crash that reading it showed. The partition invariant stays as an internal guard (`partitions`, tested on the numbers the `assert` crashed on) and cannot fire on any input. A clean tree prints nothing new: the C3 proof (272 lines, byte for byte, an EMPTY substitution list) was repeated after the change (`C4_speccheck_proof_repeated.txt`). The C3 case that pinned the assertion is replaced by five that pin the finding.

**Tests.** The Python test is the three `[historical]` cases of `tests/devtools/budgetcheck_tests.cpp` (the four wrong rows of 2026-09-18 and their corrected forms, the four refusals and the two prose cases, the rows with no arithmetic), under the ctest of the old name `budget.checker_catches_the_historical_errors`; `budgetcheck.behaviour` runs 17 more (the printed text of a run, every finding and exit code, the specification glob and its order, the refusals, the command line, the unit table, `parse_unit`'s words and quirks, `parse_number`, `parse_term`, the tolerance, and each scanner against its pattern) and `budgetcheck.real_tree` runs two (T1's shape and the row-by-row controls). 22 cases, 902 assertions. **Rule 5** (`C4_rule5_injected_defects.txt`, harness `C4_mutate_tool.sh`, list `C4_mutants.txt`): 221 defects were injected into `budgetcheck.cpp` in the first run (186 caught, one by the timeout, 23 survivors — thirteen of them thin places of the tests, each given a case, six redundant parts of the code, removed or merged, and four equivalent, said so — and eleven that did not compile or were not applied, rewritten); the whole list was run again against the final tests and the final source: **219 defects, 214 caught and one by the timeout, and none uncaught but the four equivalent ones** (`E12` and `E14`, the next place to look from after a failed start, written two ways that reach the same state; `G05`, the guard of `code_point_at`'s precondition; `O06`, the word a problem is searched for, `UNPARSEABLE` or `UNPARSE`). Twenty-seven more were injected into the changed lines of `speccheck.cpp` (the `(partial` finding and the partition guard): all caught.

**What this cannot show from here.** That the per-row lines of a non-quiet run are the Python's to the byte: no committed record of them exists to compare with (the controls and the tests are what stand for them). That the runner passes: GitHub's next run is that test, now with `TMPDIR` on a disk behind it for the whole devtools executable.

### 41.12 Group C4's follow-up — the maintainer's rulings on what reading `budgetcheck.py` showed

**The rulings** (the maintainer, 2026-10-07, on the report of group C4; made the first work of group C5, as deliberate changes of behaviour, each with a test, none to change today's results). (1) A `--spec-dir` that is absent, or holds no `SPEC-*.md`, is REFUSED as speccheck refuses it (`budgetcheck: no SPEC-*.md in DIR`, exit 2): success over nothing read is the failure this tool exists against. A directory whose specifications hold no budget row still passes: it was read. (2) Each of these silent misreadings is refused as UNPARSEABLE, exit 2, naming the row (plan §5 constraint 4: refuse rather than approximate): `10^+3`, which the Python read as 10 because the plus sign made `^+3` the dimensionless "" raised to 3 — so any power with no unit before it is refused; a unit symbol with `^` and no exponent (`m^`, read as `m`); a digit separator in an exponent (`m^1_0`, read as `m^10`); and a left side that is NaN (an infinity times zero), which passed because no comparison with NaN is true. (3) KEPT, and documented in the tool's header as what it is: the tolerance of a stated zero is 0.5 in the stated units — the stated-precision rule (half a unit of the last stated digit) read for a stated 0. The Python gave every zero the same 0.5 however many digits it is written with (`0`, `0.0` and `0.00` alike) and so does the tool; for `0.00` that is looser than the digit rule would be, recorded here and not changed. The deliberate changes of §41.11 (overflow made UNPARSEABLE, exponents above a million refused, a non-UTF-8 specification refused) were accepted.

**What did not change.** Today's results. The registered comparison of §41.11 was repeated on the new binary: the three lines of gate 8's section, byte for byte; the tool's non-quiet output on the real tree is byte-identical to the first record; the controls over every real row (ctest `budgetcheck.real_tree`) pass — so none of the refusals fires on a real row, and the default directory, which holds specifications, is not refused. **Tests:** the case that pinned the Python's pass on an empty directory is replaced by one that pins the refusal (an empty directory, an absent one, a file where a directory was meant, a directory of names that are no specification, each with and without `--quiet`, and the directory that was read and holds no row, which passes); the quirk lines of `parse_unit`'s case are replaced by the refusals and their words; a new case runs each misreading as a row (`10^+3 m`, `5 m^`, `1 m^1_0`, a NaN left side, the stated side the same way) and the forms that are accepted (`10^3`, `1e+3`, `m^1`, `m^10`); the stated zero's case gains `0.00`. **Rule 5** (`C4followup_rule5_injected_defects.txt`): the whole list regenerated, 232 defects, 228 caught and four equivalent (the same four as group C4's). **A rename:** `python_int` and `python_float`, the tool's two readers, are `py_int` and `py_float`, as the devkit's own names are (`strip_py`, `py_repr`), so that no identifier of the tree's C++ carries the word.

### 41.13 Group C5 — the three checkers and the two small tests in C++: `constraint8`, `literaturecheck`, `unitcheck`, `one_secular_pole`, `configure_is_current`

**What.** `tools/constraint8.cpp`, `tools/literaturecheck.cpp` and `tools/unitcheck.cpp` (+ `.hpp`) replace the three Python checkers; `tests/devtools/one_secular_pole.cpp` and `tests/devtools/configure_is_current.cpp` (+ `.hpp`) replace the two Python tests; `ci.sh`'s gates 9, 11 and 12 run the built tools (`$BUILD/tools/constraint8`, `literaturecheck --quiet`, `unitcheck --quiet`), the ctests `constraint8.result_only`, `tides.one_secular_pole` and `build.configure_is_current` run the built programs (the last on `CMAKE_BINARY_DIR`, as it did), and the five `.py` files are removed in the same commit. The tools are the Python's regular expressions hand-written as scanners over UTF-8 text with Python's Unicode-aware `\b`, `\s`, `\w` and `\d`, exposed so that each is tested against the semantics of the pattern it replaces: constraint8's `UNDERLYING` and `MONADIC`; unitcheck's `MARKER`, `NUMBER` (with its backtracking, its lookbehind and its lookahead), `is_thousand` (`float()` is `strtod`, over the digits of any script) and the `\bkm\b|kilomet` search with `re.I`; one_secular_pole's four `\b…\b` patterns and its window. The devkit gains `path_suffix` and `files_below` (`fs`: pathlib's `.suffix` and what `rglob("*")` finds and a tool can read, in pathlib's order) and `read_text_lossy`, `code_point_before` and `word_boundary_at` (`pytext`), each with unit cases; `files_below` and the two scanners were simplified by rule 5 (below). The shared test helper `tests/devtools/throwing_stream.hpp` makes every tool's last-resort handler (exit 70) reachable on purpose.

**The proof (D1), registered before any C++ of these tools existed** (`C5_proof_registration.txt`). None of the five writes a file. The first three PRINT, and the committed record of what they printed is the section of gate 9, 11 and 12 of every green ci run: **ten of them, on ten different trees** — the safety net `acac318`, `e0a3840`, `9067d19`, `53a1f9e`, `c7e401c`, `a584d09`, `c7969dc`, `1777172`, `19f9b39`, `7ff0964` — with counts that differ from tree to tree (constraint8: 262 to 268 files; literaturecheck: 22 entries and 297 to 304 build inputs; unitcheck: 164 sources and 30 literals, 1 + 15 + 14 + 0 + 0, on all ten), which makes the comparison stronger than C3's or C4's. The substitution list was EMPTY (none of the tools prints a path, a date or a generator name). T1: each tool, run on a `git archive` export of each of the ten commits (`--root` the export), printed the recorded section **byte for byte, exit 0, empty standard error — 30 comparisons, identical on the first run** (`C5_proof_result.txt`), and again on the final binaries (`C5_proof_final.txt`: the same 30, and the ten of T2/T3). T2/T3: the two Python tests print only when they fail or into ctest's log, so their committed record is that ctest PASSED at each of the ten commits; `one_secular_pole` exits 0 on each of the ten exports and prints, on every one, the text derived BY HAND from the Python and an independent `grep` of the four constants (`C5_expected_secular_pole_output.txt`, made before the port existed: 164 module sources, one carrying the constants scattered), and `configure_is_current` exits 0 on a fresh configure. **Independent witnesses**, made with the shell before any C++ existed: 268 source files below `modules/` and `tests/` (constraint8's count), 304 build inputs and 22 literature entries (literaturecheck's), 164 production sources and **30 literals** of value exactly 1000 or 0.001 in 15 files, by a PCRE-and-awk pipeline, with the spellings (unitcheck's).

**What the committed record does not hold, and what stands in for it.** The non-quiet listing of literaturecheck (the 22 entries) and the register of unitcheck (every literal with its file, line, spelling and annotation), and the text of every failure of all five: no log or file has them, and the Python was not run beside the port. They stand on (a) tests whose every printed text is DERIVED BY HAND from the Python's statements, (b) controls on real data — the real manifest's own id, file name and root fire literaturecheck; a copy of the real production sources is made, passes with the real output, and fails by the rule each injected defect breaks (an unannotated 1000, a UNIT-CROSSING that names kilometres, the marker two lines away; a second definition of the secular pole, a constant removed from the definition; the underlying type or a monadic call put in a module, a test or the alias header); the real tree's build system, generated in the future and at the dawn of time, passes and fails with every file named — (c) each real-tree count recounted another way (the standard directory iterator and `std::regex` in place of the hand-written scanners and files walk), (d) the FIRST record of the two non-quiet outputs on the real tree (`C5_unitcheck_register_nonquiet.txt`: 30 rows in 15 files, each read against its source line; `C5_literaturecheck_listing_nonquiet.txt`: 22 entries, 10 whose recorded terms begin `NOT ESTABLISHED`, as `grep -ci` counts them) — a regression record from now on and not a proof against the Python — and (e) rule 5.

**Differences from the Python, deliberate, each said in the tool's header and at the place.** (1) **A run that reads nothing is REFUSED, exit 2, naming the root** — constraint8 with no source, literaturecheck with no build input or no readable manifest, unitcheck and one_secular_pole with no production source, configure_is_current with no CMakeLists.txt — where the Python passed "0 files". This is the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-07 on budgetcheck applied BY ANALOGY, **not ruled for these tools: flagged for ratification**, small, tested, one line to revert each. (2) **The Python tested `"build"`, `"tests"` and `"_deps"` against the parts of the ABSOLUTE path**, so a tree that lives under a directory with one of those names silently excluded every file and passed with "0"; the ports test the path RELATIVE to the root (tested with trees under `build/deeper` and `tests/build/deeper`). No recorded result moves: no tree that was checked had such an ancestor. (3) literaturecheck visits its needles in sorted order: the Python's came out of a set, in an order that changes from run to run, so only the line order of a FAILING listing is affected. (4) A glob match or a suffix match that is no regular file (a directory called `x.cpp`, a link to nothing, a FIFO) is skipped by rule, as in speccheck (the Python's `read_text` raised); a link to a file is read, a link to a directory is not entered. (5) Where the Python read with `errors="replace"` the ports decode the same way (a byte sequence that is not UTF-8 is one U+FFFD); where it read strictly (the secular-pole test) a source that is not UTF-8 is REFUSED, exit 2, naming the file, not a traceback. (6) A manifest that is absent, not UTF-8, not JSON, with no `entries` array, with an entry that is no object, or a literature entry without a string `id` or `filename`, is REFUSED with a message (the Python crashed on each); `terms` that is no string reads as empty. (7) `--root DIR` is new on literaturecheck, unitcheck, one_secular_pole and configure_is_current (constraint8 had it): the Python took its root from the script's own place, which a test of a synthetic tree cannot use. (8) configure_is_current prints the build directory as pathlib spells it (`a//b/./c/` is `a/b/c`, the empty argument is `.`), as the Python's `{build}` did. (9) The messages name the C++ tools; argparse's abbreviations are not accepted; `-h` prints the tool's own text; an option's value is whatever follows it unless that begins with `--` (argparse also refuses one that begins with a single dash), and `-h=x` is refused. Where the Python's `.suffix` and its `rglob("*.hpp")` differ — a file called `.hpp` has no suffix but matches the glob — each port follows the Python it replaces (constraint8 the suffix; unitcheck and one_secular_pole the glob).

**Corrections of my own first drafts, kept visible.** (a) literaturecheck's `terms.upper().startswith("NOT ESTABLISHED")`: the first draft read `upper()` as the ASCII fold plus the dotless i and the long s, "the two non-ASCII letters whose upper case is ASCII". Python's `upper()` is the FULL case mapping; mapping every code point (Perl's full mapping as the witness) shows **ten** such characters (the dotless i, the long s, the sharp s, and the ff, fi, fl, ffi, ffl, long-s-t and st ligatures), of which **four** can occur in the phrase (SS, FF, FI, FL, FFI and FFL occur nowhere in it) and are the only ones mapped. (b) unitcheck's `re.I`: the first draft equated the Kelvin sign with k and the dotless i with i; Python's sre also lower-cases the capital I with a dot above to i. Every code point mapped again: those three are exactly the non-ASCII characters that come out equal to a letter of the pattern. (c) The first draft took the production sources of unitcheck and one_secular_pole by pathlib's `.suffix`; the Python's patterns are `rglob("*.hpp")` and `rglob("*.cpp")`, so a file called `.hpp` is a source (fixed, tested). (d) Where I derived a test's expectation by hand and the port disagreed, the port was right every time and the expectation was the defect: **one failed on its first run** (a four-constant example of the secular-pole scanner: I had listed the window of line 1 and not that of line 4, which has lost the first constant and so is a different list), and three more I corrected by re-deriving before any run (a secular-pole example whose two lines I had put inside the window, the line of a second window in another, and the count of a devkit case); the corrections are in the commit's tests.

**Latent defects of the Python, found by reading, kept and reported (nothing was changed for them except where said above).** (i) unitcheck's NUMBER is blind to a literal with a suffix — `1000.0f`, `1000u`, `1e3f` are no token, because a letter after the number fails the lookahead — and a `//` inside a string literal hides the rest of the line (`"http://x"`); it is a register of what the regular expression sees, not a parser. No source of the tree uses a suffixed literal (the 30 are found by an independent PCRE pipeline too). (ii) configure_is_current compares `st_mtime` as a float: at 1.7e9 seconds a double resolves 2.4e-7 s, so a CMakeLists.txt touched within about 120 ns of the generation is not seen. (iii) one_secular_pole's "two of the four within 2 lines" is a window of two lines either side of each line, so two constants up to FOUR lines apart count as adjacent. (iv) a literature entry's `terms` that is not a string, and an entry that is not an object, were tracebacks (now refusals or empty, above).

**Tests.** The five tools have no Python test but the two that were ports; everything else is NEW, because the Python tools had none: **15 cases for constraint8, 21 for literaturecheck, 22 for unitcheck, 16 for one_secular_pole and 14 for configure_is_current** (926 assertions), in `tests/devtools/*_tests.cpp`, plus 8 new devkit cases (`path_suffix`, `files_below` ×4, `read_text_lossy`, `code_point_before`, `word_boundary_at`). Each run on synthetic trees, in-process (`run` is called with captured streams): the scanners against the semantics of the regular expressions they replace, every printed text, every refusal and exit code, which files are read and in what order, universal newlines, the relative-path cases, non-regular entries and non-UTF-8 bytes, the command line, the last-resort handler (a stream whose every write throws: `throwing_stream.hpp`), and the real tree. The ctests: `constraint8.result_only` (the tool itself, as before), `tides.one_secular_pole` and `build.configure_is_current` (the programs themselves, as before), and **ten new** — `{constraint8, literaturecheck, unitcheck, secular_pole, configure_is_current}.{behaviour, real_tree}`, each selecting its tags, the selections checked with `--list-tests`. The whole devtools executable passes under a tmpfs and under a `TMPDIR` on a disk (the one skipped case is the 2^62-byte file, which ext4 will not make).

**Rule 5 (plan §4)** — one-line defects injected into a scratch copy of each source, compiled with the tree's flags (`-Werror`), linked with the tree's own unmutated test objects, the tests of the tool run once; caught = a failed assertion, a crash or the timeout (harness, generators, lists and results in the report's `C5_rule5/`, the classification of the uncaught in `C5_rule5_summary.txt`). **In the final run: 791 defects, 737 caught by a failing assertion, 15 by a crash and 4 by the timeout, and 35 were not caught, each classified equivalent or unreachable and said so** (792 lines were tried, one of which did not compile and is no defect) (constraint8 101 defects, 98 caught, 3 equivalent; literaturecheck 169, 166 caught, 3 equivalent; unitcheck 234, 217 caught, 17 equivalent; one_secular_pole 116, 111 caught, 5 equivalent; configure_is_current 100, 98 caught, 2 equivalent; the devkit's new `files_below` and `path_suffix` 41, 40 caught, 1 equivalent, and `read_text_lossy`, `code_point_before` and `word_boundary_at` 30, 26 caught, 4 equivalent). The first runs found **gaps in my tests**, each given a case (a missing `--help`, the help text itself, a file that cannot be read, the quoted line stripped in rule 8.2, `a..and_then(`, `tl:x` read as the scope, a second NBSP-before-the-colon case, the whole second against a fraction of one, the empty argument from an empty directory, a non-ASCII character standing for a blank, a letter or nothing in `terms`, a needle with a newline in it), **redundant parts of the code, removed or merged** (the early stop of the case-mapping loop; `files_below`'s directory precheck, its error-code checks and its `skip_permission_denied`, none of which the error-code iterator needs; `marker`'s unreachable fallback; `km_at`'s first assignment; unitcheck's sort, which `files_below` already does; `code_point_before`'s separate success test and `word_boundary_at`'s start guard; configure_is_current's separate existence test), and **the five mutants that had hit the wrong line** (the `ok` exit of each tool, whose anchor matched the help branch first — found by printing the line each defect hit, and re-run). The equivalent ones: guards that read the byte after the end of a string every view here is made from (`line[colon]`, `s[p]`, `s[q]`, `s[d_end]`, `i < s.size()` in `word_boundary_at`, `start > 0` in `code_point_before`), a name order that cannot matter (two names that cannot match at one place), a step by bytes where the scanner starts only at a character that is one byte, the `//` of a comment line (which the cut at `//` makes redundant, as in the Python), an initial value overwritten at once, and the one stat that can fail only if a file vanishes between two calls.

**Operative text (D6).** `SPEC-thrust-yaw.md` 1.0a names the gate as `tools/literaturecheck.cpp` (it was `.py`) in one sentence and gains a changelog section, which that specification had not got, with the 1.0a row and the 1.0 row its header already records; the comments of `core/result.hpp` (`constraint8`) and of `dynamics/force_set.hpp` (`unitcheck`, which said "gate 10", as it was when written: it is gate 12) follow the switch. **Left for C12, as at C2:** five literature entries of `manifest.json` (`terms` and `why_pinned`) say "`tools/literaturecheck.py` fails if any build input can reach it". The manifest's own hash is the workflow's cache key, so editing a sentence there would cost GitHub's next run a cache miss for a note; they follow at C12, when the manifest is touched anyway for the `python3` entry and the members' roles that still name `notice.py`. Historical prose stays: the older sections of this file, `SPEC-dynamics.md` line 57 (the history of the secular-pole test's two narrowings) and the comments of `tests/l5_exit_gate.cpp` that name the Python tools.

**What this cannot show from here.** That the non-quiet listings and the texts of failures are the Python's to the byte: no committed record exists, and the tests and controls stand for them. That the runner passes: GitHub's next run is that test. That a tree with a directory called `build` above it is checked as the Python meant: the Python's behaviour there was a defect.

### 41.14 Group C6 — a Unicode pin in place of a witness, `unitcheck`'s three blind spots, and `rk_coefficients` on the devkit's `BigInt` and `Rational`

**What.** (1) Two manifest `data` entries, `ucd-unicodedata` and `ucd-specialcasing` — `UnicodeData.txt` and `SpecialCasing.txt` of **UCD 15.1.0** (`https://www.unicode.org/Public/15.1.0/ucd/`, 1 914 200 and 16 832 bytes, sha256 `2fc713e6a31a87c4850a37fe2caffa4218180fadb5de86b43a143ddb4581fb86` and `55a477efd933a52cd27e6a9bf70265bb2d8814af31aab07767abc8eb421f27ef`), licence `Unicode-3.0` added to `tools/fetch.cpp`'s allowlist, NOTICE regenerated (119 entries); and `tests/devtools/unicode_tables_tests.cpp` on `tests/devtools/ucd_case_tables.hpp`, which DERIVE from them the facts two tools had rested on a throwaway witness for. (2) `unitcheck` reads a literal with a standard suffix, a literal with C++ digit separators, and a `//` that is not inside a string, a character literal, a raw string or a block comment, each with tests. (3) The known limits of `configure_is_current` and `one_secular_pole` are documented in their headers. (4) `tools/rk_coefficients.py` is `tools/rk_coefficients.cpp`, on two new devkit pieces, `odl/devkit/bigint.hpp` and `odl/devkit/rational.hpp` (Python's `int` and `fractions.Fraction`, as far as the tool uses them); `ci.sh`'s gate 10 runs the built tool.

**Why UCD 15.1.0, and the terms (plan §4 rule 4; read 2026-10-07, no account, nobody contacted).** The Python that produced every recorded baseline is the 3.13.15 that CMake found at `~/.local/bin/python3.13`; its documentation says of `unicodedata`: "this database is compiled from the UCD version 15.1.0" (`docs.python.org/3.13/library/unicodedata.html`). The case mappings the emulations rest on are the ones that Python's `str.upper()` and `re.IGNORECASE` carry, so that is the version pinned; nothing here claims the result for another version, and the pin makes the question answerable from bytes. **Licence.** Unicode's Terms of Use (`unicode.org/terms_of_use.html`): "Unicode Data Files" "include all computer data files under the following directories: https://www.unicode.org/Public/ ..." and "All Unicode Data Files and Unicode Software are subject to the terms and conditions of the free and open-source Unicode License v3, unless otherwise indicated by specific restriction, permission, or license identified at the point of release or in such software, data file, or other documentation"; the files' own headers (`ReadMe.txt`, dated 2023-08-28, and `SpecialCasing-15.1.0.txt`, 2023-01-05) say only "© 2023 Unicode®, Inc." and "For terms of use, see https://www.unicode.org/terms_of_use.html", so nothing at the point of release restricts further. The licence (`unicode.org/license.txt`): "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of data files and any associated documentation (the "Data Files") or software ... to deal in the Data Files or Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, and/or sell copies of the Data Files or Software ..., provided that either (a) this copyright and permission notice appear with all copies of the Data Files or Software, or (b) this copyright and permission notice appear in associated Documentation" — an MIT-class grant with one condition, which the entries meet by quoting the notice whole in their `licence_note` (and so in NOTICE); the tree redistributes none of it (pin-only, an oracle for one test), and the allowlist's reason says so. The negative control is in the report (`C6_check_licences_*`): `fetch check-licences` refused both entries (exit 3, "LICENCE NOT ON THE PERMISSIVE LIST") before the allowlist named the licence and passed after. The bytes were downloaded twice (by hand, then by `tools/fetch` into the cache) and are identical.

**What the derivation showed (registered before it was run, `C6_unicode_registration.txt`).** From the pinned files, by CPython's rules (`full_upper` = the unconditional SpecialCasing entry, else UnicodeData's simple mapping; `re.IGNORECASE` = the first code point of the full lower case, plus the table `Lib/re/_casefix.py` is made from): (P1) the non-ASCII characters whose full upper case is pure ASCII are **ten**: U+00DF, U+0131, U+017F, U+FB00–FB06 (SS, I, S, FF, FI, FL, FFI, FFL, ST, ST); (P2) the non-ASCII characters `re.IGNORECASE` equates with an ASCII letter are **four**, the four the `re` documentation names (U+0130 and U+0131 with i, U+017F with s, U+212A with k), of which three can matter to `\bkm\b|kilomet`; (P3) the whole table of extra cases so derived is **identical, entry for entry in both directions, to the 50 entries of the standard library of that Python** (`re/_casefix.py`, read as a FILE; the interpreter was not run); (P4) `literaturecheck`'s reading of `terms.upper().startswith("NOT ESTABLISHED")` and `unitcheck`'s reading of `\bkm\b|kilomet` agree with the derivation for EVERY scalar value from U+0080 to U+10FFFF (1 111 936), in 39 and 9 places respectively, black box (43 365 504 and 10 007 424 texts): no finding. The test also shows itself able to fail (tools that forget the st ligature, map the sharp s to S, forget the Kelvin sign, the dotless i, or equate the long s with i are each reported at the one character where they differ; one line removed from each pinned file changes the derived sets), and the parser refuses what is not the files' shape. `starts_not_established` is now `literaturecheck::scan::starts_not_established`, exposed for it.

**`unitcheck`: three blind spots of the Python, fixed as deliberate changes (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-07; the C5 report had found them).** NUMBER (`(?<![\w.])(\d+\.?\d*(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)(?![\w.])`) refused any number with a letter after it, and the line was cut at its first `//` wherever it stood. Now: (a) a literal with a **standard suffix** is a number — `[uU](ll|LL|l|L)?` or `(ll|LL|l|L)[uU]?` after an integer literal, `[fFlL]` after a floating one; `1000f` and `1000.0u` are not C++ and stay invisible, and so do the user-defined and library suffixes (`1000_km`, `1000ms`); (b) **digit separators** are part of the number (`1'000`, `1'000.0`, `1e1'0`: an apostrophe between two digits); (c) the comment starts at the first `//` that C++ lexes as one — not inside a string, a character literal, a raw string (prefixes `R LR uR UR u8R`, a delimiter of at most sixteen characters, over several lines) or a block comment — and a line that begins inside a string (a raw string, or one carried over by a backslash) is not a comment line even if it begins with `//` or `*`. **No finding on today's tree, from three methods:** read-only scans of the 164 production sources before any change (`C6_unitcheck_blind_spot_scans.txt`: an independent awk recount finds the register's 30 tokens, and none of the forms), the CHANGED tool's non-quiet register of the real tree equal byte for byte to the old one's (3 389 bytes, 30 literals: 1 home, 15 UNIT-CROSSING, 14 NOT-A-UNIT-CROSSING, none unaccounted, none misplaced; registered before the change), and `unitcheck --quiet` on exports of the ten commits equal byte for byte to each recorded gate-12 section (T1 repeated: the three checkers and the secular-pole test, 40 of 40). The tests: 22 cases of `unitcheck_tests.cpp` before, 34 now (591 assertions); the old expectations that DOCUMENTED a blind spot (`1000.0f`, `1000u 1000UL 1e3f 1e3L`, `1000.f`, `"http://x"; int n = 1000;`, the `f`/`u` literals of `other.cpp`) are changed by name, each with its comment saying so.

**Known limits, kept and documented (not changed without a ruling), in `unitcheck.cpp`'s header.** A line whose first non-blank characters are `//`, `*` or `/*` is skipped whole, as in the Python — a statement continued on a line that begins with `*` (a multiplication broken before its operator) is invisible; no such line holds a factor of a thousand today (a read-only scan, control: the same logic finds the register's 30 on the lines it does read). Numbers inside string literals still count (the register holds two, `normal_equations.cpp:325`, the message for 2^-1000 .. 2^1000). **Other literal forms, listed, not changed:** hexadecimal and hex-float (`0x3E8`, `0x1.F4p9`) — invisible; today's tree has only `0x1p-53`, `0x1p-1000`, `0x1p+1000`, whose last two are in the register all the same, by the digits of their exponents, so a parser that read hex would DROP those two rows (30 → 28); binary (`0b1111101000`) — invisible, none; octal (`01750` is 1000 in C++, read as 1750; `01000` is 512, read as 1000: a false negative and a false positive of the same kind) — none; a leading point (`.001`) — invisible, none (the `.6` of printf formats are in strings after a percent sign); user-defined and library suffixes (`1000_km`, `1000ms`, `1000s`) — invisible, and the units they name are exactly what a register of unit crossings would want; none; C++23 suffixes (`z`, `uz`, `f32`) — not C++20; a `//` comment continued by a backslash — the tree's `-Wall -Werror` refuses it. **`configure_is_current`'s** floats: a double holding seconds since the epoch is spaced 2^-22 s, about 238 ns, so a CMakeLists.txt newer than the generated build system by less than that can read as not newer (the check is about a configure hours old; integer nanoseconds would be a three-line change). **`one_secular_pole`'s** window: "within WINDOW lines" is two lines either side of EVERY line, so two of the four constants count as adjacent when they are at most four lines apart (the help text and the Python's docstring say "within two lines of each other"); `SPEC-perturbations` PERT-A-009, which the test serves, does not define the distance — it says only that the four constants appear nowhere in the module's source but `gravity`'s `secular_pole.hpp` — so the window is the test's own discriminator (see its header: why adjacency). Both headers say so.

**`rk_coefficients`.** The tool holds Fehlberg's Table X as `Rational`s, proves the tableau in exact arithmetic (13 rows; the 85 order conditions of c through order 7; the 200 of chat through order 8; 40 of the 115 at order 8 violated by c, which is Fehlberg's own count, from his prose) and writes the header. **The proof (D1), registered before any of it existed (`C6_rk_proof_registration.txt`):** the generated header is the SAME file (4 407 bytes, sha256 `cf282199b023dfba97ee15c72d80087ee1bc7e6c8124f3f4b3e8bafa224cdd6b`) at all ten commits whose ci runs are kept and at `ade42eb`, and gate 10 was green at each, so that file IS what the Python writes; the port, run once on an export of each of the ten, wrote it byte for byte, against a substitution list of ONE entry (line 4 names its generator, `.py` → `.cpp`), and its standard output was the five lines derived from the Python's print statements; with line 4 so changed, `--check` printed the recorded gate-10 line: **30 of 30**, on the first run. The header is regenerated (one line changed) and the first run of `rk_coefficients --check` on the tree is gate 10. **`BigInt` and `Rational`:** sign and magnitude, 32-bit limbs; division by a number of more than one limb is a bit-by-bit long division (slower than Knuth's algorithm D, with none of its rarely-taken branches, so every line of it runs on every division; the whole verification takes 20 ms); `Rational::to_double` rounds correctly (ties to even), proved against a decimal-expansion-and-`strtod` oracle, the exact ties and the bit patterns of 1/3, 2/3, 1/10, 1/5. **Where the port differs, said in the header:** `--root DIR` is new; option names are exact (argparse's abbreviations are not accepted); a header that exists and cannot be read, or cannot be written, is refused with exit 2 and the file named (the Python died with a traceback, whose status 1 it also used for "the header differs"); the sums of an elementary weight are made once per subtree rather than once per occurrence (exact arithmetic: the same numbers, fewer operations). **`Decimal` is NOT built:** nothing in this group uses it; its first consumers are C7's tools (`gradient_reference`, `legendre_reference`, `forcemodel_comparator_header`), and its semantics (context precision, `sqrt`, `**`) are best designed against what they use.

**Tests.** `tools/devkit/tests/bigint_tests.cpp` (11 cases) and `rational_tests.cpp` (7), 66 872 assertions: against values written down by hand, against 128-bit machine arithmetic on random operands (the exchange format is decimal text, so the two sides share no code), against a schoolbook multiplier on decimal digits, and against identities (`a = q·b + r`; `gcd(F(m), F(n)) = F(gcd(m, n))`); `tests/devtools/rk_coefficients_tests.cpp` (18 cases: the number of rooted trees 1, 1, 2, 4, 9, 20, 48, 115; the canonical forms and densities of the trees of orders 1 to 4 and the densities of order 5; Euler's method, the midpoint method and the classical RK4, whose order conditions are worked out by hand — RK4 satisfies all 8 through order 4 and violates all 9 of order 5 by amounts derived in the test; the proof and each of its four failures on damaged copies of the table; the header; the command line; the file; the real tree, the manifest's pin of the report and the specification); `unicode_tables_tests.cpp` (15 cases, 317 assertions). ctests `unicode_tables.parser`, `unicode_tables.derivation`, `rk_coefficients.check`, `rk_coefficients.behaviour`, `rk_coefficients.real_tree`, and every devkit case its own.

**Rule 5 (plan §4).** Defects were injected into every source of this commit that has logic — one at a time, by a generator for the operator-level kinds (a comparison turned, `&&` for `||`, `+` for `-`, a constant changed by one: `C6_rule5/harness/gen_auto.sh`), and by hand where an operator cannot reach (the suffix and separator grammar of `unitcheck`'s number, the raw-string prefixes and delimiters, the lexer's states: `gen_unitcheck_c6.sh`) — into a scratch copy that is compiled with the tree's own flags (`-Wno-error` for the defects, so that a warning of the tree's `-Werror` set is no reason for one to go unjudged), linked with the tree's own unmutated test objects, and run once; caught = a failing assertion, a crash or a timeout. Three passes, 1 936 defects in all; in the last pass of each source, on the final source: `unitcheck.cpp` 155, `literaturecheck.cpp` 171, `ucd_case_tables.hpp` 126, `devkit/bigint.cpp` 180, `devkit/rational.cpp` 37, `rk_coefficients.cpp` 197 — **866 defects: 745 caught, 78 not C++ (a type error even with `-Wno-error`: a `+` made `-` on a string), 43 not caught**, each of the 43 read and classified (`C6_rule5/classification.txt`): 40 equivalent (a `reserve` hint, a comparison inside a branch that excludes the case, an initial value that is never read, a closer that begins with a character the opener cannot hold, …) or a read one past the end of a view that changes no answer (the library's own assertions refuse it), and 3 in `rk_coefficients`'s `main()`, which the test executable does not compile and the tool's own check (`rk_coefficients --check`, which ctest and gate 10 run) catches (exit 139, 134 and 2, against 0). **Gaps the passes found became tests** — in the last pass seven defects survived that a test should have caught, four gaps (`unitcheck`: a `//` line inside a block comment, and a view whose next character in memory would change the answer, which four defects read; the Unicode reader: six- and seven-field `SpecialCasing` lines; `rk_coefficients`: a value of three dashes), and each of the seven is caught now, shown by running the defect again — or they simplified code that did nothing; a hand-injected defect that survived the first pass of `unitcheck` (an apostrophe after a number opens a character literal; a sixteen-character delimiter with a quote in it; the five raw-string prefixes each with a quote inside) is a test now. **Two hazards of the harness, met and recorded:** a defect in an argument parser made the tool write the header into files called `--check`, `--out`, `x` and `yes` in the tree's root (removed; the header was read-only during the later runs, and the test that would have written is now run with `--check`); and one defect (`ucd_65_n11`) looped and asked the kernel for 34 GB, which made 103 of its neighbours' compiles fail — they were run again under a 12 GB cap (21 real compile errors, the rest caught).

**Operative text (D6).** `SPEC-integrators.md` 1.0a (`INTG-R-001` names `tools/rk_coefficients.cpp`; a changelog row; no requirement, number or acceptance row changed); the comment of `modules/integrators/src/integrators.cpp` that named the Python; the generated header's line 4; `ci.sh`'s gate 10; the rename map above. The manifest's five notes that still name `tools/literaturecheck.py` wait for C12 (the manifest's hash is the workflow's cache key; it changed in this commit for the two new entries, which costs the next GitHub run one cache miss and a download of two files from unicode.org).

**What this cannot show from here.** That GitHub's runner can reach `www.unicode.org` (the workflow's fetch step says, on the first run; every other host it fetches from has been reachable). That the sweeps' run time (about 5 s of the devtools executable) is acceptable on the runner. That a Unicode version other than 15.1.0 would give the same ten and four: only 15.1.0 is pinned, and nothing is claimed for another.

### 41.15 Group C7 — decimal arithmetic on the devkit, `unitcheck`'s three rulings, and the four generators of the gravity and force-model numbers in C++

**What.** (1) The devkit gains **`odl/devkit/decimal.hpp`** — `Decimal`, `DecimalContext`, `LocalContext` (the part of Python's `decimal` module, libmpdec, that the generators use) — and its `BigInt` gains **Knuth's algorithm D** (long division by a number of more than one limb) and **`BigInt::isqrt`**. (2) `unitcheck` carries the maintainer's three rulings of 2026-10-07: the fourth blind spot fixed (a line is skipped only if the lexer says it is comment), hexadecimal, hexadecimal-float, binary and octal literals read as C++ reads them, and user-defined and library suffixes a visible category of their own. (3) `tools/gradient_reference.py`, `tools/forcemodel_fd_sizing.py`, `tools/forcemodel_comparator_header.py` and `tools/legendre_reference.py` are `tools/<stem>.cpp`, on the devkit's `BigInt`, `Rational` and `Decimal`; the Legendre header gets, for the first time, a ctest that regenerates it (`gravity.legendre_reference_header_matches_its_generator`).

**`Decimal`: what is claimed, from what sources, against what oracles (registered before the code, `C7_proof_registration.txt` part A).** For the operations the tools use — `+ - * /`, unary `+` and `-`, `abs`, `sqrt`, the power with an INTEGER exponent, `log10`, the comparisons, truth, `float()`, `str()` and `format()` with the types e, E, f, F — `Decimal` gives, in the current context (precision, ROUND_HALF_EVEN, Emax/Emin of Python's default; a local context and a changed precision as the tools use them), the same coefficient, exponent and **sign of a zero** as Python 3.13's `decimal`. Not claimed: NaN, infinities, subnormals, the other rounding modes, a non-integer power, `ln` and `exp`; anything outside throws (`DecimalError` and its subclasses), as Python raises. **Sources (plan §4 rule 4; read 2026-10-07, no account):** the documentation of the module (`docs.python.org/3.13/library/decimal.html`) and the General Decimal Arithmetic Specification (`speleotrove.com/decimal/decarith.html`: the ideal exponent of a quotient and of a root, the sign of a zero result, the rounding of every operation). **libmpdec's source was NOT read**: the integer power, which is libmpdec's and not "correctly rounded" (square-and-multiply in a working precision of `prec + digits(exponent) + exponent + 2` digits, one more for a negative exponent, rounded to the context at the end), is written from what the author knew of it, and prediction P-D1 below is its witness. **Oracles, none of them `Decimal` itself:** exact rational arithmetic (the correctly rounded result of `+ - * /` and the square root is the exact value rounded once: 6,000 random rounds at 1 to 40 digits), GNU bc 1.07.1 (a host tool used to derive digits, never by the build: `sqrt(2)`, `sqrt(5)`, `ln(10)`, `log10` at seven precisions), the specification's own examples, and `BigInt::isqrt` with its remainder test. `tools/devkit/tests/decimal_tests.cpp`: 20 cases, 219,941 assertions (most of them the 40,000 additions and subtractions of the boundary test that rule 5 asked for); the tests of `BigInt` grew by four cases (Knuth D on operands of limbs 0, 1 and all-ones, the six hand-listed add-back rows found by a counting search, a thousand-digit division, `isqrt` exhaustively to 70,000 and on 300 random numbers): 15 cases, 270,279 assertions, the bit-by-bit division of group C6 kept in the tests as the oracle.

**P-D1, the witness of the integer power, registered before any of it ran:** SPEC-gravity §4.7 records, for `gradient_reference.py --check` over its 145 cases, "worst relative disagreement 5.9 × 10⁻⁸⁴" — the size of the ROUNDING NOISE of a chain of decimal operations at 90 digits (divisions, roots, products, `r ** 3`, `(1/r) ** n`, `r ** (-s)`), which only arithmetic that rounds exactly where libmpdec rounds can reproduce. The port printed **5.888E-84** on its first run: the prediction holds, and the tests of the real tree pin it (between 5.85 and 5.95 × 10⁻⁸⁴).

**The proofs of the four generators (D1), registered before any of the C++ existed, each run ONCE on its first working build** (the results are `C7_gradient_reference_proof_result.txt`, `C7_forcemodel_fd_sizing_proof_result.txt`, `C7_comparator_and_legendre_proof_result.txt`):

| tool | the committed artefact | substitution list (registered) | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gradient_reference --header` | `modules/gravity/tests/gradient_reference.hpp`, 25,539 bytes, 171 lines, 145 tensors, sha256 `a7f7ef81a80ca241881bc3c1f58d0febb6fa5d5730197d559b9420d7d526a1a0` | line 1: `tools/gradient_reference.py` → `.cpp` | **byte for byte** (0.12 s) |
| `forcemodel_fd_sizing --check` and `--scan` | the L7 report's `forcemodel_fd_sizing_check.out` (2,088 bytes, sha256 `4fc032a5…c0ee`) and `…_scan.out` (2,502 bytes, `9a5c36bc…6cad`), the outputs of the Python, tied to the tree by §40.6's hashes | **empty** (the output names no tool) | **byte for byte**, both (0.003 s and 0.8 s) |
| `forcemodel_comparator_header --header` | `modules/forcemodel/tests/comparator_polynomials.hpp`, 5,499 bytes, 139 lines, `09913db6…157afe` | line 1 and line 15: `tools/forcemodel_comparator_header.py` and `(tools/forcemodel_fd_sizing.py)` → `.cpp` | **byte for byte** |
| `legendre_reference --header` | `modules/gravity/tests/legendre_reference.hpp`, 7,969 bytes, 113 lines, 78 values, `b92e8b77…352f6bee` | line 1: `tools/legendre_reference.py` → `.cpp` | **byte for byte** (2.2 s) |

The three headers are regenerated in this commit (four lines changed in all: the generator's own name; the sizing has none). **What stands on tests and not on a record:** the usage and refusals of every tool, the two-precision guards' REFUSED texts, the missing coefficient file (exit 2), the MISMATCH of a frozen number, the `--verify` texts. The proof was repeated on the final sources, after the changes that rule 5 caused (built with `CXX=g++-13` they regenerate the three headers identically (25,540, 5,501 and 7,970 bytes), print the sizing's two outputs at 2,088 and 2,502 bytes (sha256 `4fc032a5…` for the check), print `5.888E-84` over the 145 cases, and pass 163 cases with 493,430 assertions, as the g++ 15 build does: `C7_final_binary_checks.txt`).

**Where the generators differ from the Python, deliberately.** `gradient_reference`: a polynomial's value at a point (a double, so a rational with a power of two below it) is a sum of integers over one common denominator, made once, where the Python made a `Fraction` of every term; the polynomials of a coefficient are made once and not for each of the ten evaluations; the dict's insertion order is kept (`Poly`), because `forcemodel_fd_sizing` sums over it in floating point. `forcemodel_fd_sizing`: every floating-point operation is the Python's, in its order and not fused (`-ffp-contract=off`); `float ** int` is the C library's `pow()` called through a pointer the compiler cannot fold; `math.radians` and `math.degrees` are `x * (π/180)` and `x * (180/π)` as CPython computes them; `sum()` of three floats is **CPython 3.12's compensated (Neumaier) sum** (the recorded `--scan` depends on it); the coefficient file is read once; a missing file is exit 2 after the eight lines that need none (the Python's docstring promised 2 and its code raised, exit 1). `legendre_reference`: the sum of the definition is evaluated by Horner's rule in u² and its integer coefficients by the ratio of consecutive ones (exact), in place of `x ** e` for every term — at 9,460 digits that is a hundred times faster, and the 60-digit values it emits do not depend on the order, which the comparison with the committed file shows; the two-precision guard is unchanged and a test makes it REFUSE (sixty digits at degree 60 order 0 lose eighteen of them); `--verify` is new. `--root DIR` is new for `forcemodel_fd_sizing`, the only tool that reads a file of the tree. The Python's argparse took any unambiguous abbreviation of an option; here the names are exact.

**`unitcheck`: the three rulings (the maintainer's, 2026-10-07; registered as P-U1 to P-U3).** (1) The lexer returns the SPANS of code of each line; numbers are looked for in them; a line that begins with `*` outside a comment is code, and so is what follows a block comment on the line it ends on; a line inside a block comment is comment whole. A line above is a marker's place when its comment has nothing but blanks before it (the two flags that said "begins inside a string or a block comment" were deleted in this group: the end of the string or of the block is something before the comment, so the rule already refuses them — found by rule 5 as nine survivors with one cause). (2) Hexadecimal (`0x3E8`), binary (`0b1111101000`), octal (`01750` is 1000, `01000` is 512) and hexadecimal-float (`0x1.F4p9`, computed exactly and rounded once, equal to 1000.0 or 0.001 as a double) literals are read with C++'s digit separators and standard suffixes; **the two rows of the register that existed only through the exponent digits of `0x1p-1000` and `0x1p+1000` (`modules/estimation/src/normal_equations.cpp` lines 16 and 17) LEAVE it: 30 → 28 literals, 14 → 12 "not conversions", the correction of a misreading, both rows named**. (3) A literal with a user-defined suffix (an underscore and a name) or a library one (`h min s ms us ns d y i il if`) is listed in a section of its own, counted in the total, never judged (none today). **P-U1 (the register of the real tree, `C7_unitcheck_register_diff.txt`): exactly the registered difference and no other**; **P-U2: the quiet output on `git archive` of each of the ten commits whose ci logs are kept equals that commit's recorded gate-12 section after the same three changes, 10 of 10, repeated on the final binary and on the g++-13 one.** Still invisible, and not in the ruling: a literal that begins with a point (`.001`; none today).

**Rule 5 (plan §4), under a memory cap this time.** Every defect was compiled and run under `ulimit -v` (4 GB for the compiler, 3 GB for the test executable) and at most four at a time (`C7_rule5/harness`): the lesson of group C6's one defect that asked the kernel for 34 GB.
