### 41.16 Group C7b — the ten ILRS orbit files vendored, and `fetch` extracts the members of a vendored archive

**Why.** GitHub's run 37535688772 (group C6's push) failed at the fetch, in the step that populates the cache from origin, not in a gate: the ten `ilrs-lageos1-sp3-260103*` entries (the ILRS combined weekly orbit of LAGEOS-1 and the nine centres' products of the same week, `.sp3.gz`, pinned at L6 step 4) came back from `edc.dgfi.tum.de` to the runner as an HTML page, and a cache cannot be saved by a failed job. Group C7's push would have failed the same way; the maintainer's order (2026-10-07, relaying the user's approval) was to vendor the ten pinned files RAW under the existing vendored mechanism before C7 is pushed. This is the same shape as C1b's (`PROVENANCE.md` §41.3: four entries left unvendored for eighteen days while GitHub's workflow failed on every run): an origin that serves a developer's machine and not the runner cannot be fetched on a clean clone, whatever its pin says.

**What was done.** (1) `manifest/manifest.json`: `"vendored": true` on the ten entries; the bytes are tracked at `data/vendored/<id>/<filename>`, **2,418,532 bytes in all (2.3 MiB; the stop was 20 MB)**, copied from the cache after each one's SHA-256 was re-checked against its pin (all ten equal; `cmp` equal to the cache copies); in each entry the sentence of the licence note that said the tree did not redistribute the file now says it VENDORS it, raw and byte for byte as pinned, on the basis of the statement already quoted (the ILRS's citation page: "The data and products are not copyrighted; however, ... we request that you include the following citation", the quotation of the SLRF2020 entries, which is unchanged), which is neither a licence grant nor a restriction, the citation requested being carried in the entry and in NOTICE; one sentence is appended to each `upstream_mutable_note` (why, when, that the bytes are the pinned ones). Licence `ILRS-PUBLIC` unchanged. (2) **`tools/fetch.cpp`**, because vendoring alone does not do what the tests need: the tests read the EXTRACTED member at `data/cache/<id>/extracted/<member>` (`modules/io` and `modules/measmod` CMake, `tools/measmod_reference.py`), and the vendored branch of `fetch_entry` stopped at the hash check; only a cached archive had its declared members extracted. A clean clone would have had the tracked gzip and no `.sp3` to read. Now the vendored branch also extracts the declared `extract` members from the TRACKED archive into the cache (nothing is downloaded, each member against its own hash, a second `fetch` says `cached`), and `verify` tells a vendored entry whose TRACKED file is missing ("restore from git", all that helps) from one whose member is merely not extracted yet (`fetch` does that, offline; the verdict is then the general "not in the cache. Run: tools/bootstrap.sh" and not "`fetch fetch` will not help"). The other vendored entries have no member to extract and print what they printed. (3) `tests/devtools/fetch_tests.cpp`, one case: the extraction from the tracked copy and its idempotence, `--refresh`, a wrong member hash refused with nothing left behind, a member not marked `extract` left in place, a missing tracked file told from a member not extracted (alone and with one of each), a changed tracked file refused before anything is extracted; and the devkit case that reads every pinned member out of its real archive (`tools/devkit/tests/archive_tests.cpp`), which looked for every archive in the cache, now reads a vendored one at its tracked path -- the one test of 737 that failed in the first rehearsal of the runner's cache (without the ten files), which a cache that has them could not show. (4) `manifest/MANIFEST.md`: the `vendored` row and a paragraph of the Vendoring section. (5) `NOTICE`, regenerated by `tools/notice` (119 entries; ten paragraphs changed, by the sentence replaced and nothing else).

**Registered before the change** (`C7b_proof_registration.txt`; results `C7b_proof_result.txt`), each checked once: **P-V1** the ten files total 2,418,532 bytes and each is its pin and its cache copy: yes. **P-V2** `fetch fetch --keep-going` on an export whose cache holds everything except the ten entries, the network poisoned: the ten report `vendored`, their members are extracted (the hash of each printed), nothing is downloaded, a second run says `cached`, `verify` is clean, and the ten extracted members are **byte-identical (`cmp`, 10 of 10) to the files that were in the cache before**. **P-V3, the control:** the fetch built from the tree BEFORE the change, on the same export and the new manifest, extracts nothing (no directory in the cache for any of the ten) and `verify` then says, for ten entries whose tracked file is there, "vendored -- restore from git, do not fetch" and "10 vendored entries are missing their own tracked file(s). `fetch fetch` will not help -- restore from git": **vendoring alone would have left a clean clone red, with a message that sends it the wrong way.** **P-V4** the G5 consumers cannot move: their inputs are byte-identical (P-V1, P-V2); the full assertion listings of `odl_io_tests` (79 cases, 40,994 assertions) and `odl_measmod_tests` (77 cases, 17,929) are the same, byte for byte after the pointer values are masked, before and after (`C7b_g5_consumers_before.txt`, `C7b_g5_consumers_after.txt`); and `ci.sh --prove-offline` from an isolated export whose cache lacks the ten entries and whose first act is the workflow's own `fetch fetch` passes (the report). **P-V5** NOTICE changes in the ten paragraphs only: yes (ten hunks). **P-V6** rule 5 on the changed lines of `fetch.cpp`: 14 defects (operators and texts of the changed lines, six by hand), 13 caught by the fetcher's tests, one not C++; two of them survived the first draft of the test (the member's printed hash was not read, and "cached" was matched as a prefix) and the test now reads both.

**What this cannot show from here.** Whether GitHub's runner then passes the fetch: the other hosts it reaches may refuse it in their turn (every group of this step found one), and only the next run says. The pinned bytes themselves are what the EDC served on 2026-10-05/06; nothing here proves what its host serves on another day, and the tracked copy no longer depends on it.

### 41.17 CI's Python off — the user's decision of 2026-10-08

**The decision.** The user, 2026-10-08, relayed by the maintainer: *"Stop CI's Python now"*; the user's question, verbatim: *"why the executor is still running python??"* The transitional safety net of §41.1 — `ci.sh`, ctest and the configure running the Python tools that groups C8 to C11 had not yet rewritten — is OVER. From this commit **nothing runs Python: not an agent, not `ci.sh`, not ctest, not the configure, not GitHub.** The checks that only Python performed are switched OFF until their C++ replacements land, and `ci.sh` says so in its last line. A tool of this tree that has no C++ yet is not run by anything; it stays in the tree as the text a port is written from, and is removed by the group that replaces it.

**What this commit changes** (the build and CI files only; no source, test, number or acceptance row):
1. `CMakeLists.txt`: `find_package(Python3 3.9 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Interpreter)`, which RAN the interpreter on every configure to read its version, is gone. A `find_package` of Python or Perl is refused (`CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_*`), and a READ of `Python3_EXECUTABLE`, `Python_EXECUTABLE`, `Python2_EXECUTABLE`, `PYTHON_EXECUTABLE` or `PERL_EXECUTABLE` is a FATAL ERROR of the configure that names the file that read it (`variable_watch`). Nothing references them now.
2. `tests/CMakeLists.txt`: the seven ctests that ran a `.py` are removed, each named in a plain comment at its place with the group that brings it back. **Back with group C8, in C++, under the same name:** `measmod.registry_facts_reproduce`, `measmod.fd_sizing_reproduces`, `measmod.reference_header_matches_its_generator`, `measmod.height_sensitivity_prediction_reproduces`, `measmod.g5_selection_reproduces`. **Back with group C9:** `estimation.sizing_header_matches_generator`, `estimation.spec_table_matches_generator` (acceptance condition §41.8).
3. `tools/ci.sh`: the `PY` variable is gone. **Gate 13 (the build is reproducible, `tools/reprocheck.py`) does not run** until its C++ replacement (group C11); the script prints `gate 13 (reproducible build): OFF until its C++ replacement (C11), by the user's decision of 2026-10-08`, and its last line says what ran: `12 of 13 gates passed; gate 13 (reproducible build) is OFF` — never "all".
4. `tools/bootstrap.sh`: no change (it ran no Python; it ends in `ci.sh`).
5. `.github/workflows/rewrite-ci.yml`: the `actions/setup-python` step and its comment (a TRANSITIONAL pin of CPython 3.13, there because `tools/estimation_sizing.py` printed figures that depended on the interpreter's float summation: run 37485373306 of 2026-10-06 failed exactly that one test on the runner's 3.11) are gone.

**What is NOT checked while these are off** (said plainly, so that no green tick is read as more): (a) the reproducibility of the build (two builds into different directories give the same artefacts) — C11; (b) that the committed `modules/measmod/tests/measmod_reference.hpp` is what its generator writes, that the specification's registry counts, finite-difference sizing, height sensitivity and G5 selection are what their generators print — C8 (the numbers themselves are unchanged and the module tests that consume them still run); (c) that the committed `modules/estimation/tests/registered_figures.hpp` and the table of `SPEC-estimation.md` are what `tools/estimation_sizing.py` prints — C9. The Python files of (b) and (c) and `reprocheck.py` stay in the tree, unrun, as the text their ports are written from.

**The proof that nothing runs Python.** `PYOFF_proof.txt` in the report's files: `ci.sh --prove-offline` from an isolated `git archive` export of this commit, `TMPDIR` on a disk, CI's compiler, with a directory of STUBS first on `PATH` — `python`, `python3` and `perl`, shell scripts that append their invocation to a log and exit 1 — **the log stayed empty and `ci.sh` exited 0** (12 of 13 gates passed; gate 13 off); the fresh `CMakeCache.txt` holds no `Python3_EXECUTABLE`; the stubs are shown to work (an invocation is logged), and the guard is shown to fire (a ctest that reads `Python3_EXECUTABLE` makes the configure fail, naming the file); and a grep of the build and CI files finds no interpreter invocation left (the only lines that name one are the guard itself and CALCEPH's own `ENABLE_PYTHON OFF`).

**What this cannot show from here.** That GitHub's next run is green (the maintainer verifies and pushes). That nothing on the runner's own system starts an interpreter — `apt-get` of the image runs maintainer scripts and triggers of its own, which this tree does not control and the stubs on `ci.sh`'s `PATH` do not cover; what is shown is that nothing of THIS tree does.

**Addendum, the same day: the `python3` host-tool entry of the manifest is RETIRED** (the maintainer's ruling, on the proof above). The manifest declared a build-host tool `python3` (">=3.9", PSF-2.0, "runs tools/fetch.py, tools/notice.py and tools/speccheck.py at build time"): its role text had been false since groups C1 to C3 replaced those three tools, and gate 1, which lists every entry, printed `host python3 >=3.9 (not fetched: provided by the build host)` to every reader of a run — a record that says the build needs Python, which the user's decision rules out. It is removed from `manifest/manifest.json` (119 entries to 118), `NOTICE` is regenerated (it loses the row `python3 >=3.9 PSF-2.0 tool` and nothing else), and `PSF-2.0` leaves the licence allowlist of `tools/fetch.cpp` (no other entry used it: checked). Constraint 9 (plan §5): gate 1 (the manifest verifies offline) and gate 2 (every licence is permissive) were re-run on the result and print what they printed before less that entry; no pin, hash, cached byte or number moved. The manifest's hash is the workflow's cache key, so GitHub's next run misses the cache once and downloads again (accepted). The shim proof of this section was repeated on this commit (`PYOFF_proof_manifest.txt`): empty stub log, exit 0, no `Python3_EXECUTABLE` in the fresh cache.

### 41.18 Group C7c — the two IGS final orbit files vendored, and `fetch --replace-stale` with the workflow's `restore-keys`

**Why.** GitHub's run 37730732165 (the push of 2154101, the commit that retired the `python3` entry) was red in the step that populates the cache from origin, not in a gate. 2154101 changed `manifest/manifest.json` (the `python3` entry retired), whose hash is the cache key, so the cache missed and every pinned entry was fetched from its origin again; the connection to `igs.bkg.bund.de` port 443 timed out after 30,000 ms for the two IGS final orbit files (`igs-final-sp3-2023-022` and `-023`; curl 28) and then the TLS handshake was dropped (curl 35, "unexpected eof"), though the same host had served the same two files to the runner in run 37571132052. Two weaknesses, one order (the maintainer's, 2026-10-08, relaying the user's approval for L0 step 8): **(1)** an origin that serves a developer's machine and not the runner cannot be fetched on a clean clone, whatever its pin says (C1b, §41.3; C7b, §41.16), so the two files are vendored; **(2)** a change of the manifest was a cold cache, and a cold cache needs some twenty hosts and ninety-odd entries to answer in the same twenty minutes, so the workflow's cache step restores the newest earlier cache (`restore-keys`).

**A premise of the order, corrected.** The order assumed that a file restored from an earlier manifest's cache and no longer matching its pin "is refetched by rule". It is not: `fetch_entry` hashes a cached file and, when it is not the pin, REFUSES it (`mismatch()`: HASH MISMATCH, exit 2), and the workflow's retry loop treats exit 2 as final. `restore-keys` alone would therefore have turned every legitimate change of a pin into a red run — worse than the failure it cured, and invisible until the first such change. Found by reading `fetch_entry` before the workflow was edited; the maintainer agreed and approved `--replace-stale` as specified below (an option, used by the workflow's populate step alone; not a looser default: the refusal stays what it was everywhere else).

**What was done.** (1) *The two files vendored, RAW:* `data/vendored/igs-final-sp3-2023-022/IGS0OPSFIN_20230220000_01D_15M_ORB.SP3.gz` (97,869 bytes, SHA-256 f7f1df60…) and `…-023/IGS0OPSFIN_20230230000_01D_15M_ORB.SP3.gz` (97,823 bytes, 28ee14d5…), 195,692 bytes in all, copied after each was re-hashed from the cache against its pin and compared (`cmp`) equal to the cache copy (P-V1). `"vendored": true` on both entries; the sentence of each `licence_note` that said the tree did not redistribute the file now says it VENDORS it. The origin's terms (read 2026-10-06; the document is pinned as the literature entry `igs-2020-data-product-terms-of-use`): the IGS data and products "have been made openly available for use without restriction" and "continue to be offered free of cost or obligation", with an attribution term and a disclaimer. That is an unrestricted grant of USE that does not name redistribution, and the reading is written into each `licence_note` in plain words, as the policy of `MANIFEST.md` asks for that case (Vallado's package is filed under it): *redistribution implied, not stated* — copying a file is a use, no term of the document restricts it, and the data centres that mirror these files do the same; the attribution is carried in the entry and in NOTICE, the disclaimer is quoted. The reading is made under the policy and is flagged for the maintainer's ratification. Licence `IGS-PUBLIC` unchanged; the `upstream_mutable_note` of each says why and when. `NOTICE` regenerated (118 entries; two hunks, the two paragraphs). 21 entries are vendored now. The members are read as before: `fetch` extracts each file's one declared member into `data/cache/<id>/extracted/` from the tracked archive (the code of C7b). No build file or test reads the two entries yet (`SPEC-estimation.md` names them as `IGSFIN`), so no number can move. (2) *`fetch fetch --replace-stale`* (`tools/fetch.cpp`): a cached file whose SHA-256 is not the entry's pin is reported on a line that begins `stale` (the entry's id; the first sixteen hex digits of what the file holds and of the pin), removed, and then met as a file that was never there: downloaded, the download verified against the pin as ever, so upstream drift is still refused, with the same HASH MISMATCH text, word for word (a test compares the two). The same for an extracted archive member that is not its declared hash (`  stale  <member>`, removed, taken out again of the archive, which was verified a moment before), on all three roads to a member: the cached archive, the archive downloaded just now, and the TRACKED archive of a vendored entry. A file that is the pin is neither touched nor named; a vendored entry's tracked file is never replaced (a changed one is refused, as before). **Without the flag nothing changes:** a cached file that is not its pin is the refusal it was, and a stale member is taken out again quietly, as it always was (a test for each of the three roads). The flag belongs to `fetch` alone, takes no value, and is refused together with `--refresh` (exit 2, argparse's code): `--refresh` asks whether upstream still serves the pin and leaves the cache alone, the other mends the cache to the pin, and a command that did both would answer neither. After a network failure the stale file is already gone, so the workflow's retry loop finds a file that is not there and has nothing stale to say. (3) *The workflow:* `restore-keys: manifest-` in the cache step and `--replace-stale` in the populate step, each with a comment that says the two are one change and why (the step that restores and the step that mends); 15 lines added and one changed, nothing else (P-V9). `tools/ci.sh` and every local `fetch` refuse as before. (4) *Tests and documents:* four fetcher cases (the flag on files; drift, a network failure and the retry; the members on the three roads with and without the flag; the command line and the help text), 106 assertions: `[fetcher]` is 31 cases and 590 assertions (27 and 484 before). `manifest/MANIFEST.md` (the vendoring paragraphs, the policy bullet, the command table, a paragraph on the flag), the header comment and the help text of `fetch.cpp`.

**Registered before the change** (`C7c_proof_registration.txt`; results `C7c_proof_result.txt`), each run once. **P-V1** the two files are their pins and equal the cache copies: 2 of 2. **P-V2** constraint 9 (plan §5), gates 1 and 2 with the tool and manifest of 2154101 and with the new ones over the same cache: exit 0 in all four; `check-licences` byte-identical (27 lines); `verify` 199 lines each and different in exactly two, the paths of the two entries (`data/cache/<id>/…` became `data/vendored/<id>/…`; the hash is the same). The first comparison diffed the raw outputs of two exports whose roots differ, so every line that prints a path differed; the registered statement was read from the same saved outputs with the roots replaced by `<ROOT>`, declared in the result file, nothing re-run. **P-V3** an export of the new tree whose cache lacks the two entries, the network poisoned twice (proxies to a closed port, and a `curl` first on `PATH` that logs and fails): exit 0 twice, no call of curl, both entries `vendored`, their members extracted (`941697da…`, `530343f0…`), `cached` the second time, and **byte-identical (`cmp`) to the members that were in the real cache**. **P-V4**, the control: the tool and manifest of 2154101 over the same cache: exit 4, curl called twice, "2 of 94 entries did not make it", the two ids — the failure of run 37730732165, made on this machine. **P-V5** NOTICE: one file, two hunks, 118 entries in the manifest. **P-V6** `--replace-stale` on the real tree with the real network, on two NIST files of 1,347 and 1,608 bytes (one changed in its first byte, one absent): the plain `fetch` refuses the changed one (exit 2, HASH MISMATCH, file untouched); with the flag, exit 0, one `stale` line naming it (`ce0eeeb8…` is not the pin `a71c2810…`), both files downloaded and `ok`, 71 `cached`, both `cmp` equal to the real cache's; a second run names nothing and downloads nothing. **P-V9** the workflow differs from 2154101's by the 15 added lines and the one changed command.

**Rule 5** (plan §4) on the changed lines of `fetch.cpp` (the helper, the signature and the three call sites, the option, the command line, the help text), a frozen g++ 13 build, 15 mechanical and string defects and 33 made by hand (negations, a removed statement, swapped arguments, wrong widths, the words of the `stale` line: what the generators cannot make). First pass: 48 defects; 43 caught by an assertion, one by the harness's timeout (below), two that do not compile (`"literal" - std::string`: no such program), and **two survivors, both gaps in my tests**: `args.replace_stale` replaced by `true` on the vendored road and on the downloaded road names a stale member although the flag was not given; I had tested "without the flag nothing changes" on the cached road only. Two steps added to the members case; second pass: 48 defects, **46 caught, 2 not compilable, 0 survivors**, the unmutated build green (`C7c_rule5/`).

**An incident of the first pass.** The defect that removes the refusal of `--replace-stale` with `--refresh` turned my command-line case into a real `fetch --refresh`: the case called the tool bare, that is on THIS tree's manifest and cache. It re-downloaded part of the real cache — eight files (`erfa`, `catch2`, `calceph`, `tl-expected`, `eopc04`, `tn36-chapter5`, `tn36-chapter8`, `de440s`), each checked against its pin before it replaced the identical copy, so no byte changed — and was cut off by the timeout in the ninth (`de440t.bsp`, whose `.part` file I removed); and a defect that made the tool accept a flag it should refuse ran a plain `fetch` on the real tree, which rewrote `data/cache/receipts.json` (the same pins, new timestamps). `fetch verify` of the real tree afterwards: exit 0, every entry. Nothing was lost, but a test of a REFUSAL must not depend on the refusal to keep its hands off the real tree: the case now runs on a scratch tree with the stand-in curl, and the second pass ran with `data/cache` and `data/literature` read-only (restored by a trap).

**The shim proof of §41.17 is repeated on this commit** (stubs for `python`, `python3` and `perl` first on `PATH`, `TMPDIR` on a disk, CI's compiler): its log is in the report's files (`C7c_ci_*.log`), with the stub log, which is not empty if anything started an interpreter.

**What this cannot show from here.** That GitHub's next run is green: BKG is out of its path, but the exact cache key misses once more (the manifest changed), `restore-keys` restores the newest cache that an earlier GREEN run saved, if GitHub still holds one (it evicts caches not used for seven days), and without one the run is a cold cache like the runs before it, which now needs only the other hosts. That `actions/cache` restores a prefix, reports `cache-hit` false for it and saves under the new key as its documentation says (read, not run: a workflow cannot be run here), and that the populate step then runs `fetch --replace-stale` in the order the comments describe. That the workflow parses: the diff is of comments, two lines of a step's keys and one command, read by eye.
